rationale:
Split into 3 children forming the chain smooth_cutoff_seq → restrict_eq_of_smooth_test → setintegral_eq_preimage; the parent uses only the last one directly. The supplied proof bundles three standard, independently reusable facts: (1) the smooth Urysohn exhaustion of an open set from step 3; (2) steps 3–4: finite measures with equal integrals of C_c^∞ tests supported in U have equal restrictions to U (dominated convergence, then π-system uniqueness); (3) steps 1, 2 and 4: the hypothesis ∫_U b u = ∫ (b∘q) h dσ upgrades to ∫_B u = ∫_{q⁻¹B} h dσ for measurable B ⊆ U. This is exactly the parent's σ₁ = σ₂ evaluated on B, i.e. λ₊(B) + m₋(B) = λ₋(B) + m₊(B).

How the children give the parent through the supplied proof (steps 0, 5–7). Let ũ be a measurable version of u on U (step 0, needed for u only) and E := toMeasurable volume (q '' A).
- Step 5: for measurable B' ⊆ U ∖ E we have q⁻¹B' ⊆ Aᶜ, so σ(q⁻¹B') = 0 and ∫_{q⁻¹B'} h dσ = 0. Child (3), applied with hq.measurable, then gives ∫_{B'} ũ = ∫_{B'} u = 0, which is step 5's λ₊(B') = λ₋(B').
- Step 6: on B'₊ = (U∖E) ∩ {ũ > 0}, integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg_ae forces volume(B'₊) = 0; the same argument for −ũ handles B'₋ = (U∖E) ∩ {ũ < 0}.
- Step 7: B ∩ {u ≠ 0} ⊆ (B ∩ E) ∪ B'₊ ∪ B'₋ ∪ (U ∩ {u ≠ ũ}), and the last set is Lebesgue-null (Measure.restrict_apply'). Hence volume(B ∩ {u ≠ 0}) ≤ volume(B ∩ E) = volume(B ∩ q '' A) by measure_union_le and Measure.measure_toMeasurable_inter_of_sFinite.
This assembly was compiled in Lean against the byte-identical frozen parent type, using only child (3) and no sorry.

Why split instead of proving it in one block: the node is at depth 5 with max_depth 6, so the children are forced leaves, and every leaf must be a single appended theorem with no helper declarations. The split replaces a monolith of about 270 lines with independent proofs of about 65, 32 and 92 lines, each a standard lemma (C_c^∞ exhaustion; uniqueness of finite measures from smooth tests; a distributional-to-setwise identity for a density against a push-forward).

Statement choices: (3) assumes only Measurable q (the parent supplies Continuous.measurable) and omits σ univ < ∞, which its proof never uses. (2) concludes μ.restrict U = ν.restrict U for arbitrary finite μ and ν, so it needs no 'carried by U' hypothesis.

subproblems.title: Smooth compactly supported cutoffs converging pointwise to the indicator of an open set
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and let V ⊆ ℝⁿ (= Euclid n) be open. Then there is a sequence (b_j)_{j∈ℕ} of functions b_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ with the following properties. For every j, b_j is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)), b_j has compact support, tsupport b_j ⊆ V, and 0 ≤ b_j(y) ≤ 1 for all y. For every y ∈ ℝⁿ, b_j(y) → 1_V(y) as j → ∞, where 1_V is the indicator function of V.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid n)), IsOpen V → ∃ b : ℕ → Euclid n → ℝ, (∀ j, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (b j)) ∧ (∀ j, HasCompactSupport (b j)) ∧ (∀ j, tsupport (b j) ⊆ V) ∧ (∀ j y, 0 ≤ b j y ∧ b j y ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ y, Tendsto (fun j => b j y) atTop (𝓝 (V.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) y))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the cutoff construction in step 3 of the parent proof (K_j, r_j, smooth Urysohn functions b_j), stated for an arbitrary open set V ⊆ ℝⁿ = Euclid n.
1. (Compact exhaustion.) For j ∈ ℕ put K_j := {y ∈ ℝⁿ : (j+1)⁻¹ ≤ infEDist(y, ℝⁿ ∖ V)} ∩ closedBall(0, j), where infEDist is the [0,∞]-valued infimum distance (Metric.infEDist) and (j+1)⁻¹ is computed in [0,∞]. The map y ↦ infEDist(y, Vᶜ) is continuous (Metric.continuous_infEDist), so the first set is closed (isClosed_le against a constant). closedBall(0, j) is compact (isCompact_closedBall). Hence K_j is compact (IsCompact.inter_left).
2. (K_j ⊆ V.) Let y ∈ K_j and suppose y ∉ V. Then y ∈ Vᶜ, so infEDist(y, Vᶜ) = 0 (Metric.infEDist_zero_of_mem), and (j+1)⁻¹ ≤ 0 in [0,∞], i.e. (j+1)⁻¹ = 0. But (j+1)⁻¹ > 0 because j+1 ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.inv_pos). This is a contradiction, so K_j ⊆ V.
3. (Every point of V lies in K_j for all large j.) Let y ∈ V. As V is open, Vᶜ is closed, so y ∉ Vᶜ = closure(Vᶜ) and therefore infEDist(y, Vᶜ) > 0 (Metric.infEDist_pos_iff_notMem_closure; if V = ℝⁿ the infimum over ∅ is ∞). Since (j+1)⁻¹ → 0 in [0,∞] (ENNReal.tendsto_inv_nat_nhds_zero composed with j ↦ j+1, tendsto_add_atTop_nat), eventually (j+1)⁻¹ < infEDist(y, Vᶜ). Choose N ∈ ℕ with ‖y‖ ≤ N (exists_nat_ge). For j ≥ N, dist(y, 0) = ‖y‖ ≤ N ≤ j, i.e. y ∈ closedBall(0, j). Hence y ∈ K_j for all sufficiently large j.
4. (Radii.) Fix j. K_j is compact and contained in the open set V (step 2), so there is δ_j > 0 with cthickening(δ_j, K_j) ⊆ V (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Put r_j := δ_j / 2 > 0; then cthickening(2 r_j, K_j) ⊆ V.
5. (Smooth Urysohn functions.) The set thickening(2 r_j, K_j) is open (isOpen_thickening), cthickening(r_j, K_j) is closed (isClosed_cthickening), and cthickening(r_j, K_j) ⊆ thickening(2 r_j, K_j) because 0 < 2 r_j and r_j < 2 r_j (cthickening_subset_thickening'). Since ℝⁿ is a finite-dimensional real normed space, exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff (with smoothness parameter ⊤ : ℕ∞) gives b_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ such that: b_j is ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞); range b_j ⊆ [0, 1]; support b_j = thickening(2 r_j, K_j); and for every x, x ∈ cthickening(r_j, K_j) ↔ b_j(x) = 1. Choose such r_j and b_j for every j (choice over j ∈ ℕ).
6. (Support and range.) tsupport b_j = closure(support b_j) = closure(thickening(2 r_j, K_j)) ⊆ cthickening(2 r_j, K_j) (closure_thickening_subset_cthickening) ⊆ V (step 4). The set cthickening(2 r_j, K_j) is compact because K_j is compact and ℝⁿ is proper (IsCompact.cthickening), and tsupport b_j is closed (isClosed_tsupport). So tsupport b_j is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset), i.e. HasCompactSupport b_j, and tsupport b_j ⊆ V. Since range b_j ⊆ [0, 1], 0 ≤ b_j(y) ≤ 1 for all y.
7. (Pointwise convergence.) Let y ∈ ℝⁿ.
- If y ∈ V, then 1_V(y) = 1. By step 3, for all large j we have y ∈ K_j ⊆ cthickening(r_j, K_j) (self_subset_cthickening), hence b_j(y) = 1 by step 5. The sequence (b_j(y)) is eventually constant equal to 1, so it converges to 1 = 1_V(y) (tendsto_const_nhds.congr').
- If y ∉ V, then 1_V(y) = 0. For every j, b_j(y) ≠ 0 would give y ∈ support b_j ⊆ tsupport b_j ⊆ V (subset_tsupport and step 6), which is impossible. So b_j(y) = 0 for every j, and the sequence converges to 0 = 1_V(y).
This proves all five properties. ∎

It compiles without `sorry` and uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
```lean
theorem Submission.cbr_ci_pw_noi_smooth_cutoff_seq : ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid n)), IsOpen V → ∃ b : ℕ → Euclid n → ℝ, (∀ j, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (b j)) ∧ (∀ j, HasCompactSupport (b j)) ∧ (∀ j, tsupport (b j) ⊆ V) ∧ (∀ j y, 0 ≤ b j y ∧ b j y ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ y, Tendsto (fun j => b j y) atTop (𝓝 (V.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) y)) := by
  intro n V hV
  -- compact exhaustion `K j = {y : infEDist y Vᶜ ≥ 1/(j+1)} ∩ closedBall 0 j`
  set K : ℕ → Set (Euclid n) := fun j =>
    {y | ((j : ℝ≥0∞) + 1)⁻¹ ≤ infEDist y Vᶜ} ∩ closedBall 0 j with hK
  have hKc : ∀ j, IsCompact (K j) := fun j =>
    (isCompact_closedBall 0 (j : ℝ)).inter_left (isClosed_le continuous_const continuous_infEDist)
  have hKV : ∀ j, K j ⊆ V := by
    intro j y hy
    by_contra hyV
    have h1 : ((j : ℝ≥0∞) + 1)⁻¹ ≤ infEDist y Vᶜ := hy.1
    rw [infEDist_zero_of_mem hyV] at h1
    exact (ENNReal.inv_pos.mpr (by simp)).ne' (le_antisymm h1 bot_le)
  have hKev : ∀ y ∈ V, ∀ᶠ j in atTop, y ∈ K j := by
    intro y hy
    have hpos : 0 < infEDist y Vᶜ := by
      rw [infEDist_pos_iff_notMem_closure, hV.isClosed_compl.closure_eq]
      exact fun h => h hy
    have h1 : ∀ᶠ j : ℕ in atTop, ((j : ℝ≥0∞) + 1)⁻¹ ≤ infEDist y Vᶜ := by
      have ht : Tendsto (fun j : ℕ => ((j : ℝ≥0∞) + 1)⁻¹) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
        have := ENNReal.tendsto_inv_nat_nhds_zero
        exact (this.comp (tendsto_add_atTop_nat 1)).congr (fun j => by simp)
      filter_upwards [ht.eventually (gt_mem_nhds hpos)] with j hj using hj.le
    have h2 : ∀ᶠ j : ℕ in atTop, y ∈ closedBall (0 : Euclid n) j := by
      obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := exists_nat_ge ‖y‖
      filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop N] with j hj
      rw [mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right]
      exact hN.trans (by exact_mod_cast hj)
    filter_upwards [h1, h2] with j hj1 hj2 using ⟨hj1, hj2⟩
  -- radii with `cthickening (2 r) (K j) ⊆ V`
  have hr : ∀ j, ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ cthickening (2 * r) (K j) ⊆ V := by
    intro j
    obtain ⟨δ, hδ, hsub⟩ := (hKc j).exists_cthickening_subset_open hV (hKV j)
    exact ⟨δ / 2, by positivity, by rwa [mul_div_cancel₀ _ two_ne_zero]⟩
  choose r hr0 hrV using hr
  -- smooth Urysohn functions
  have hb : ∀ j, ∃ f : Euclid n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f ∧ range f ⊆ Icc 0 1 ∧
      support f = thickening (2 * r j) (K j) ∧ ∀ x, x ∈ cthickening (r j) (K j) ↔ f x = 1 := by
    intro j
    exact exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff isOpen_thickening isClosed_cthickening
      (cthickening_subset_thickening' (by linarith [hr0 j]) (by linarith [hr0 j]) _)
  choose b hbsmooth hbrange hbsupp hbone using hb
  have htsupp : ∀ j, tsupport (b j) ⊆ cthickening (2 * r j) (K j) := by
    intro j
    rw [tsupport, hbsupp]
    exact closure_thickening_subset_cthickening _ _
  refine ⟨b, hbsmooth, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro j
    exact (hKc j).cthickening.of_isClosed_subset (isClosed_tsupport _) (htsupp j)
  · intro j
    exact (htsupp j).trans (hrV j)
  · intro j y
    exact hbrange j ⟨y, rfl⟩
  · intro y
    by_cases hy : y ∈ V
    · rw [indicator_of_mem hy]
      apply tendsto_const_nhds.congr'
      filter_upwards [hKev y hy] with j hj
      exact ((hbone j y).mp (self_subset_cthickening _ hj)).symm
    · rw [indicator_of_notMem hy]
      apply tendsto_const_nhds.congr'
      filter_upwards with j
      by_contra hne
      exact hy ((htsupp j).trans (hrV j) (subset_tsupport _ (Ne.symm hne)))
```
proof_key_steps: Compact exhaustion K_j := {y : infEDist(y, Vᶜ) ≥ (j+1)⁻¹} ∩ closedBall(0, j): each K_j is compact, K_j ⊆ V, and every y ∈ V lies in K_j for all large j.
Radii r_j > 0 with cthickening(2r_j, K_j) ⊆ V (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open).
Smooth Urysohn function b_j (exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff): values in [0,1], support = thickening(2r_j, K_j), and b_j = 1 exactly on cthickening(r_j, K_j).
tsupport b_j ⊆ cthickening(2r_j, K_j), which is compact and contained in V.
b_j(y) is eventually 1 for y ∈ V and identically 0 for y ∉ V, so b_j → 1_V pointwise.

subproblems.title: Finite measures with equal integrals of smooth test functions supported in U agree on U
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝⁿ be open, and let μ, ν be finite Borel measures on ℝⁿ. Suppose ∫ b dμ = ∫ b dν for every b : ℝⁿ → ℝ that is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)), has compact support and satisfies tsupport b ⊆ U. Then the restrictions agree: μ⌞U = ν⌞U (μ.restrict U = ν.restrict U).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid n)) (μ ν : Measure (Euclid n)), IsOpen U → IsFiniteMeasure μ → IsFiniteMeasure ν → (∀ b : Euclid n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) b → HasCompactSupport b → tsupport b ⊆ U → ∫ y, b y ∂μ = ∫ y, b y ∂ν) → μ.restrict U = ν.restrict U
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–4 of the parent proof (dominated convergence along smooth cutoffs of O ∩ U, then uniqueness of finite measures from the π-system of open sets). In the parent, σ₁ = μ₁⌞U and σ₂ = μ₂⌞U. Here the argument is run for arbitrary finite μ and ν, and the conclusion is stated for their restrictions to U, so no "carried by U" hypothesis is needed.
1. (Cutoffs for O ∩ U.) Let O ⊆ ℝⁿ be open and put V := O ∩ U; V is open, hence Borel measurable. By the sibling theorem Submission.cbr_ci_pw_noi_smooth_cutoff_seq applied to V, there are b_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ (j ∈ ℕ), each ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) with compact support, tsupport b_j ⊆ V and 0 ≤ b_j ≤ 1, such that b_j(y) → 1_V(y) for every y ∈ ℝⁿ.
2. (Limits of the test integrals.) Let ρ be any finite measure on ℝⁿ. Each b_j is continuous, hence a.e.-strongly measurable; |b_j(y)| ≤ 1 for all j and y; the constant function 1 is ρ-integrable because ρ is finite (integrable_const); and b_j → 1_V pointwise everywhere. By dominated convergence (tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence with bound 1), ∫ b_j dρ → ∫ 1_V dρ = ρ.real(V) = (ρ V).toReal (integral_indicator_one, V measurable).
3. (μ and ν agree on O ∩ U.) Because tsupport b_j ⊆ V ⊆ U and b_j is smooth with compact support, the hypothesis gives ∫ b_j dμ = ∫ b_j dν for every j. By step 2 for ρ = μ and ρ = ν, this single real sequence converges both to μ.real(V) and to ν.real(V). By uniqueness of limits (tendsto_nhds_unique), μ.real(V) = ν.real(V). As μ(V) < ∞ and ν(V) < ∞, μ(V) = ν(V) (ENNReal.toReal_eq_toReal_iff' with measure_ne_top). Thus μ(O ∩ U) = ν(O ∩ U) for every open O.
4. (The restrictions agree on open sets and on ℝⁿ.) For open O, (μ⌞U)(O) = μ(O ∩ U) and (ν⌞U)(O) = ν(O ∩ U) (Measure.restrict_apply, O measurable), so (μ⌞U)(O) = (ν⌞U)(O) by step 3. Taking O = ℝⁿ gives (μ⌞U)(ℝⁿ) = μ(U) = ν(U) = (ν⌞U)(ℝⁿ) (Measure.restrict_apply_univ).
5. (Uniqueness.) The open subsets of ℝⁿ form a π-system (isPiSystem_isOpen). It generates the σ-algebra of ℝⁿ, which is the Borel σ-algebra borel ℝⁿ = generateFrom {open sets} (BorelSpace.measurable_eq). The measure μ⌞U is finite since μ is. Two measures, the first finite, that agree on a generating π-system and on the whole space coincide (MeasureTheory.ext_of_generate_finite with C = {s | IsOpen s}). By step 4, μ⌞U = ν⌞U. ∎

It compiles without `sorry` and uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
```lean
theorem Submission.cbr_ci_pw_noi_restrict_eq_of_smooth_test : ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid n)) (μ ν : Measure (Euclid n)), IsOpen U → IsFiniteMeasure μ → IsFiniteMeasure ν → (∀ b : Euclid n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) b → HasCompactSupport b → tsupport b ⊆ U → ∫ y, b y ∂μ = ∫ y, b y ∂ν) → μ.restrict U = ν.restrict U := by
  intro n U μ ν hU hμ hν htest
  -- the two measures agree on `O ∩ U` for every open `O`
  have hopen : ∀ O : Set (Euclid n), IsOpen O → μ (O ∩ U) = ν (O ∩ U) := by
    intro O hO
    obtain ⟨b, hbs, hbc, hbt, hb01, hblim⟩ :=
      Submission.cbr_ci_pw_noi_smooth_cutoff_seq n (O ∩ U) (hO.inter hU)
    have hlim : ∀ ρ : Measure (Euclid n), IsFiniteMeasure ρ →
        Tendsto (fun j => ∫ y, b j y ∂ρ) atTop (𝓝 (ρ.real (O ∩ U))) := by
      intro ρ hρ
      rw [← integral_indicator_one (hO.inter hU).measurableSet]
      refine tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence (fun _ => (1 : ℝ))
        (fun j => (hbs j).continuous.aestronglyMeasurable) (integrable_const 1)
        (fun j => Eventually.of_forall fun y => ?_) (Eventually.of_forall hblim)
      rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_le]
      constructor <;> linarith [(hb01 j y).1, (hb01 j y).2]
    have heq : ∀ j, ∫ y, b j y ∂μ = ∫ y, b j y ∂ν := fun j =>
      htest (b j) (hbs j) (hbc j) ((hbt j).trans inter_subset_right)
    have h1 := hlim μ hμ
    have h2 := hlim ν hν
    simp_rw [heq] at h1
    exact (ENNReal.toReal_eq_toReal_iff' (measure_ne_top _ _) (measure_ne_top _ _)).mp
      (tendsto_nhds_unique h1 h2)
  -- uniqueness of finite measures agreeing on the π-system of open sets
  have := hμ
  refine ext_of_generate_finite {s | IsOpen s} BorelSpace.measurable_eq isPiSystem_isOpen ?_ ?_
  · intro s hs
    have hs' : IsOpen s := hs
    rw [Measure.restrict_apply hs'.measurableSet, Measure.restrict_apply hs'.measurableSet]
    exact hopen s hs'
  · rw [Measure.restrict_apply_univ, Measure.restrict_apply_univ]
    simpa using hopen univ isOpen_univ
```
proof_key_steps: For open O and V := O ∩ U, take the sibling cutoffs b_j → 1_V (smooth, compact support, tsupport b_j ⊆ V ⊆ U, 0 ≤ b_j ≤ 1).
Dominated convergence with bound 1 (finite measure): ∫ b_j dρ → ρ(V) for ρ = μ and ρ = ν.
The hypothesis gives ∫ b_j dμ = ∫ b_j dν, so μ(O ∩ U) = ν(O ∩ U) (finite values) for every open O, including O = ℝⁿ.
μ⌞U and ν⌞U agree on the π-system of open sets generating the Borel σ-algebra and on ℝⁿ, so ext_of_generate_finite gives μ⌞U = ν⌞U.

subproblems.title: A smooth-test identity between a density and a pushed-forward measure holds on Borel subsets of U
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝⁿ open, u : ℝⁿ → ℝ Lebesgue integrable on U, σ a (Borel) measure on ℝ^P, q : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ measurable and h : ℝ^P → ℝ σ-integrable. Assume ∫_U b(y)u(y)dy = ∫ b(q(x))h(x)dσ(x) for every C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) compactly supported b : ℝⁿ → ℝ with tsupport b ⊆ U. Then ∫_B u(y)dy = ∫_{q⁻¹(B)} h(x)dσ(x) for every measurable B ⊆ U.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid n)) (u : Euclid n → ℝ) (σ : Measure (Euclid P)) (q : Euclid P → Euclid n) (h : Euclid P → ℝ), IsOpen U → Measurable q → IntegrableOn u U → Integrable h σ → (∀ b : Euclid n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) b → HasCompactSupport b → tsupport b ⊆ U → ∫ y in U, b y * u y = ∫ x, b (q x) * h x ∂σ) → ∀ B : Set (Euclid n), MeasurableSet B → B ⊆ U → ∫ y in B, u y = ∫ x in q ⁻¹' B, h x ∂σ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 2 and 4 of the parent proof (σ₁, σ₂ built from u^± Lⁿ⌞U and q_*(h^∓σ), equality of their test integrals, uniqueness), evaluated on a measurable B ⊆ U. Measurable representatives (parent step 0) are not needed here, because the withDensity lemmas below only require a.e.-measurable densities. Finiteness of σ is not used: the push-forward measures are finite because h is integrable.
1. (Four finite measures.) Write ofReal : ℝ → [0,∞]; recall ofReal(t) = ofReal(max(t, 0)) and (ofReal t).toReal = max(t, 0) (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal'). Define:
- λ₊ := (Lⁿ⌞U).withDensity(y ↦ ofReal(u y)) and λ₋ := (Lⁿ⌞U).withDensity(y ↦ ofReal(−u y));
- m₊ := q_*(σ.withDensity(x ↦ ofReal(h x))) and m₋ := q_*(σ.withDensity(x ↦ ofReal(−h x))), where q_* = Measure.map q.
These are u⁺Lⁿ⌞U, u⁻Lⁿ⌞U, q_*(h⁺σ) and q_*(h⁻σ). Since u and −u have finite integral for Lⁿ⌞U, and h and −h have finite σ-integral, the four withDensity measures are finite (isFiniteMeasure_withDensity_ofReal). Push-forwards of finite measures are finite (Measure.isFiniteMeasure_map). Put μ₁ := λ₊ + m₋ and μ₂ := λ₋ + m₊; both are finite measures on ℝⁿ.
2. (Integrals against these measures.)
(a) If f is integrable on U, then for every b : ℝⁿ → ℝ, ∫ b d((Lⁿ⌞U).withDensity(ofReal ∘ f)) = ∫_U max(f(y), 0) b(y) dy. Indeed, the density ofReal ∘ f is a.e.-measurable for Lⁿ⌞U (f is a.e.-strongly measurable) and everywhere finite, so integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀ applies, and (ofReal f(y)).toReal = max(f(y), 0).
(b) If g is σ-integrable and b is continuous, then ∫ b d(q_*(σ.withDensity(ofReal ∘ g))) = ∫ b(q x) d(σ.withDensity(ofReal ∘ g))(x) (integral_map: q is measurable, and b, being continuous, is a.e.-strongly measurable). By the same withDensity lemma this equals ∫ max(g(x), 0) b(q(x)) dσ(x).
3. (Equal integrals of test functions.) Let b : ℝⁿ → ℝ be ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) with compact support and tsupport b ⊆ U. Then b is continuous with compact support, hence bounded, |b| ≤ C (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support), and integrable for every finite measure (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). By integral_add_measure and step 2 (with f = u, −u and g = h, −h):
- ∫ b dμ₁ = ∫_U max(u, 0) b dy + ∫ max(−h, 0)·(b∘q) dσ;
- ∫ b dμ₂ = ∫_U max(−u, 0) b dy + ∫ max(h, 0)·(b∘q) dσ.
The integrands are integrable: max(±u, 0) is Lⁿ⌞U-integrable (Integrable.pos_part / Integrable.neg_part) and b is bounded and measurable (Integrable.mul_bdd); likewise max(±h, 0)·(b∘q) is σ-integrable, since b∘q is bounded and measurable. Since max(t, 0) − max(−t, 0) = t (max_zero_sub_max_neg_zero_eq_self), integral_sub gives:
- ∫_U max(u, 0) b − ∫_U max(−u, 0) b = ∫_U b u;
- ∫ max(h, 0)(b∘q) dσ − ∫ max(−h, 0)(b∘q) dσ = ∫ (b∘q) h dσ.
By hypothesis ∫_U b u = ∫ (b∘q) h dσ. Combining these four real identities linearly, ∫ b dμ₁ − ∫ b dμ₂ = ∫_U b u − ∫ (b∘q) h dσ = 0, i.e. ∫ b dμ₁ = ∫ b dμ₂.
4. (Uniqueness on U.) By the sibling theorem Submission.cbr_ci_pw_noi_restrict_eq_of_smooth_test (U open, μ₁ and μ₂ finite, step 3), μ₁⌞U = μ₂⌞U. Let B ⊆ U be measurable. Then μ_i(B) = μ_i(B ∩ U) = (μ_i⌞U)(B) (Measure.restrict_apply, B ∩ U = B). Hence λ₊(B) + m₋(B) = λ₋(B) + m₊(B) (Measure.add_apply), an identity between finite numbers.
5. (Evaluation on B.) For measurable B ⊆ U:
- λ_±(B) = ∫⁻_B ofReal(±u) dLⁿ (withDensity_apply, then Measure.restrict_restrict: (Lⁿ⌞U)⌞B = Lⁿ⌞(B ∩ U) = Lⁿ⌞B);
- m_±(B) = σ.withDensity(ofReal ∘ (±h))(q⁻¹B) = ∫⁻_{q⁻¹B} ofReal(±h) dσ (Measure.map_apply with q and B measurable, then withDensity_apply with q⁻¹B measurable).
6. (Conclusion.) u is integrable on B (as B ⊆ U) and h is integrable on q⁻¹B. So by integral_eq_lintegral_pos_part_sub_lintegral_neg_part and step 5:
- ∫_B u dy = λ₊(B).toReal − λ₋(B).toReal;
- ∫_{q⁻¹B} h dσ = m₊(B).toReal − m₋(B).toReal.
Applying toReal to the identity of step 4 (ENNReal.toReal_add, all four values finite by measure_ne_top) gives λ₊(B).toReal + m₋(B).toReal = λ₋(B).toReal + m₊(B).toReal. Therefore ∫_B u dy = λ₊(B).toReal − λ₋(B).toReal = m₊(B).toReal − m₋(B).toReal = ∫_{q⁻¹B} h dσ. ∎

Formalization note: in Lean, `∫ y in U, f y - ∫ y in U, g y` parses with the subtraction inside the first integrand, because the integrand is parsed at precedence 60 and `-` has precedence 65. Write `(∫ y in U, f y) - ∫ y in U, g y` instead. The frozen type `∫ y in B, u y = ∫ x in q ⁻¹' B, h x ∂σ` is unaffected because `=` has precedence 50.

Appendix (reference only): a Lean script of exactly this argument. It was checked with `lake env lean` after `import GMT.Ch07.Submission`, inside `namespace GMT.Ch07` with the frozen contract's `open`s (project b4d606db, Mathlib 25730c7c), inserted before `main_theorem` and after the sibling theorems. It compiles without `sorry` and uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
```lean
theorem Submission.cbr_ci_pw_noi_setIntegral_eq_preimage : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid n)) (u : Euclid n → ℝ) (σ : Measure (Euclid P)) (q : Euclid P → Euclid n) (h : Euclid P → ℝ), IsOpen U → Measurable q → IntegrableOn u U → Integrable h σ → (∀ b : Euclid n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) b → HasCompactSupport b → tsupport b ⊆ U → ∫ y in U, b y * u y = ∫ x, b (q x) * h x ∂σ) → ∀ B : Set (Euclid n), MeasurableSet B → B ⊆ U → ∫ y in B, u y = ∫ x in q ⁻¹' B, h x ∂σ := by
  intro P n U u σ q h hU hq hu hh htest B hB hBU
  -- the four finite measures `λ±` and `m±`
  set lp : Measure (Euclid n) := (volume.restrict U).withDensity fun y => ENNReal.ofReal (u y)
    with hlp
  set lm : Measure (Euclid n) := (volume.restrict U).withDensity fun y => ENNReal.ofReal (-u y)
    with hlm
  set mp : Measure (Euclid n) := (σ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (h x)).map q with hmp
  set mm : Measure (Euclid n) := (σ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (-h x)).map q with hmm
  have hlpf : IsFiniteMeasure lp := isFiniteMeasure_withDensity_ofReal hu.2
  have hlmf : IsFiniteMeasure lm := isFiniteMeasure_withDensity_ofReal hu.neg.2
  have hmpf : IsFiniteMeasure mp := by
    have : IsFiniteMeasure (σ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (h x)) :=
      isFiniteMeasure_withDensity_ofReal hh.2
    exact Measure.isFiniteMeasure_map _ _
  have hmmf : IsFiniteMeasure mm := by
    have : IsFiniteMeasure (σ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (-h x)) :=
      isFiniteMeasure_withDensity_ofReal hh.neg.2
    exact Measure.isFiniteMeasure_map _ _
  -- integrals of a test function against `λ±` and `m±`
  have hlam : ∀ (f : Euclid n → ℝ) (b : Euclid n → ℝ), IntegrableOn f U →
      ∫ y, b y ∂((volume.restrict U).withDensity fun y => ENNReal.ofReal (f y)) =
        ∫ y in U, max (f y) 0 * b y := by
    intro f b hf
    rw [integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀ hf.aemeasurable.ennreal_ofReal
      (Eventually.of_forall fun _ => ENNReal.ofReal_lt_top)]
    simp only [ENNReal.toReal_ofReal', smul_eq_mul]
  have hpush : ∀ (g : Euclid P → ℝ) (b : Euclid n → ℝ), Integrable g σ → Continuous b →
      ∫ y, b y ∂((σ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (g x)).map q) =
        ∫ x, max (g x) 0 * b (q x) ∂σ := by
    intro g b hg hb
    rw [integral_map hq.aemeasurable hb.aestronglyMeasurable,
      integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀ hg.aemeasurable.ennreal_ofReal
        (Eventually.of_forall fun _ => ENNReal.ofReal_lt_top)]
    simp only [ENNReal.toReal_ofReal', smul_eq_mul]
  -- equal integrals of test functions
  have hkey : ∀ b : Euclid n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) b → HasCompactSupport b → tsupport b ⊆ U →
      ∫ y, b y ∂(lp + mm) = ∫ y, b y ∂(lm + mp) := by
    intro b hb hbc hbU
    have hbcont : Continuous b := hb.continuous
    obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := hbcont.bounded_above_of_compact_support hbc
    have hbm : AEStronglyMeasurable b (volume.restrict U) := hbcont.aestronglyMeasurable
    have hbqm : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => b (q x)) σ :=
      (hbcont.measurable.comp hq).aestronglyMeasurable
    rw [integral_add_measure (hbcont.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport hbc)
        (hbcont.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport hbc),
      integral_add_measure (hbcont.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport hbc)
        (hbcont.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport hbc),
      hlam u b hu, hlam (fun y => -u y) b hu.neg, hpush h b hh hbcont,
      hpush (fun x => -h x) b hh.neg hbcont]
    have I1 : (∫ y in U, max (u y) 0 * b y) - ∫ y in U, max (-u y) 0 * b y =
        ∫ y in U, b y * u y := by
      have hsub := integral_sub (hu.pos_part.mul_bdd hbm (Eventually.of_forall hC))
        (hu.neg_part.mul_bdd hbm (Eventually.of_forall hC))
      refine hsub.symm.trans (integral_congr_ae (Eventually.of_forall fun y => ?_))
      simp only
      rw [← sub_mul, max_zero_sub_max_neg_zero_eq_self, mul_comm]
    have I2 : ∫ x, max (h x) 0 * b (q x) ∂σ - ∫ x, max (-h x) 0 * b (q x) ∂σ =
        ∫ x, b (q x) * h x ∂σ := by
      have hsub := integral_sub (hh.pos_part.mul_bdd hbqm (Eventually.of_forall fun x => hC (q x)))
        (hh.neg_part.mul_bdd hbqm (Eventually.of_forall fun x => hC (q x)))
      refine hsub.symm.trans (integral_congr_ae (Eventually.of_forall fun x => ?_))
      simp only
      rw [← sub_mul, max_zero_sub_max_neg_zero_eq_self, mul_comm]
    have := htest b hb hbc hbU
    linarith
  -- uniqueness: the two measures agree on subsets of `U`
  have hres := Submission.cbr_ci_pw_noi_restrict_eq_of_smooth_test n U (lp + mm) (lm + mp) hU
    inferInstance inferInstance hkey
  have hBeq : (lp + mm) B = (lm + mp) B := by
    have := congrArg (fun μ : Measure (Euclid n) => μ B) hres
    simpa only [Measure.restrict_apply hB, inter_eq_left.mpr hBU] using this
  -- evaluate the four measures on `B`
  have hlB : ∀ f : Euclid n → ℝ, ((volume.restrict U).withDensity fun y => ENNReal.ofReal (f y)) B =
      ∫⁻ y in B, ENNReal.ofReal (f y) := by
    intro f
    rw [withDensity_apply _ hB, Measure.restrict_restrict hB, inter_eq_left.mpr hBU]
  have hmB : ∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ, ((σ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (g x)).map q) B =
      ∫⁻ x in q ⁻¹' B, ENNReal.ofReal (g x) ∂σ := by
    intro g
    rw [Measure.map_apply hq hB, withDensity_apply _ (hq hB)]
  rw [Measure.add_apply, Measure.add_apply] at hBeq
  have hreal : (lp B).toReal + (mm B).toReal = (lm B).toReal + (mp B).toReal := by
    rw [← ENNReal.toReal_add (measure_ne_top _ _) (measure_ne_top _ _),
      ← ENNReal.toReal_add (measure_ne_top _ _) (measure_ne_top _ _), hBeq]
  -- convert to real integrals
  have hL : ∫ y in B, u y = (lp B).toReal - (lm B).toReal := by
    rw [integral_eq_lintegral_pos_part_sub_lintegral_neg_part (hu.mono_set hBU), hlp, hlm, hlB, hlB]
  have hR : ∫ x in q ⁻¹' B, h x ∂σ = (mp B).toReal - (mm B).toReal := by
    rw [integral_eq_lintegral_pos_part_sub_lintegral_neg_part hh.integrableOn, hmp, hmm, hmB, hmB]
  rw [hL, hR]
  linarith
```
proof_key_steps: λ± := (Lⁿ⌞U).withDensity(ofReal(±u)) and m± := q_*(σ.withDensity(ofReal(±h))) are finite measures; set μ₁ := λ₊ + m₋ and μ₂ := λ₋ + m₊.
For smooth compactly supported b with tsupport b ⊆ U: ∫ b dμ₁ − ∫ b dμ₂ = ∫_U b u − ∫ (b∘q) h dσ = 0 (withDensity and map integral formulas, u = u⁺ − u⁻, h = h⁺ − h⁻).
The sibling uniqueness lemma gives μ₁⌞U = μ₂⌞U, so λ₊(B) + m₋(B) = λ₋(B) + m₊(B) for measurable B ⊆ U.
λ±(B) = ∫⁻_B ofReal(±u) and m±(B) = ∫⁻_{q⁻¹B} ofReal(±h) dσ; writing each integral as positive part minus negative part yields ∫_B u = ∫_{q⁻¹B} h dσ.
